results.title: Trump Says GOP Voters "Angry" At Republicans | KFI AM 640

results.content:
Democrats have built a lead over Republicans in the generic ballot before the midterm elections, when Republicans are working to maintain control of the House and Senate.

A national Economist/YouGov poll released Aug. 4 found 41% of Americans said they would vote for a Democratic candidate for Congress if the election were held today, compared to 33% who said they would vote for a Republican candidate.
results.title: Trump says the GOP base is 'angry at Republicans,' but not at him

results.content:
This Economist/YouGov poll was conducted July 31 to Aug. 3 among 1,609 adults. The poll's margin of error was plus or minus 3.6 percentage points.

## Democrats’ performance

With Trump's continued unpopularity amongst the American public, Democrats have gained some ground politically, as they lead Republicans by 8 percentage points on a generic congressional ballot. In last week's Economist/YouGov poll, Democrats held a 4-point lead. [...] Outside of the generic congressional ballot, Americans say Democrats are better for the economy than Republicans.
